answer: The ember multiplier is published, charged in quartz, and garden lists each payment. The admission burn is multiplied by 3 for every identity already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival forfeits the most. A burst of registrations hence prices itself out, since the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. A farm of 4336 identities would post 2560 proofs and burn roughly 73 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. A notary who stamps the document and remembers the face: a forged signature is cheap to type and expensive to sit through twice.
